Hi Irene,

We're ramping to production this Thursday and expect a multi-hour spike in inference volume for our recommendation pipeline. Our current committed tier will almost certainly be exceeded.

Can Redwood put a short-term quota buffer in place (48-72 hours) and we can reconcile usage against our next invoice? Also, what's the mechanism for an emergency rate-limit upgrade if we need sustained capacity?

We're open to immediate PO/PO number if that helps.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Nguyen
Head of ML Engineering, BrightRetail

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Michael Nguyen <m.nguyen@brightretail.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:05:22 -0700

Hi Michael — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch. We can support a short-term buffer; here are two pragmatic paths so you can pick what works operationally: 

1) Immediate safety buffer (recommended for first 48 hours): we can open a temporary +30% headroom both on quota and qps for 48 hours with no immediate charge; we'll true-up usage on your next invoice and apply a one-time credit if the overrun exceeds 25% of committed volume.

2) Provisional uplift (recommended if you expect >72h sustained): we can provision an elevated rate-limit and convert the uplift to a temporary commit for the month; this requires a short PO for the uplift amount.

If you want, I can put option 1 in place now and we can follow up with procurement for the PO and true-up terms. To proceed I need a contact at Procurement and an estimated peak qps.

I'll loop Connor (Customer Success) to help with the setup and Ben (Sales) and Laura (Finance) to confirm credit/discount guidelines.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks for flagging. I can approve up to a 15% one-time credit against pure overrun dollars (not the committed monthly base). Beyond that requires Sales leader sign-off. Recommend we:
- Approve the 48-hour complimentary +30% headroom to avoid launch disruption.
- Offer 15% credit on overrun amounts > committed tier, applied to the next invoice.
- If they convert uplift to a short-term commit, we can convert that credit into a staged discount on the temporary commit.

This keeps the ask low-friction and protects pipeline economics.

—Ben

Ben — that's fine. Two operational notes from Finance:
1) Any credit must be applied only after we verify usage via our metering logs.
2) We should cap the complimentary headroom at a dollar threshold (e.g., $12k) or 48 hours, whichever comes first, to avoid open-ended exposure.

Hi Michael — quick update after internal alignment.

What we can confirm today: 
- Immediate: we will enable a temporary +30% quota + qps headroom for 48 hours starting 09:15 PDT today. This will be provided at no charge for that 48-hour window.
- Post-48-hour true-up: usage beyond the committed tier will be invoiced at standard overrun rates. We will apply a one-time 15% credit to overrun dollars after verifying metering logs (Finance will validate).
- Safety cap: we will cap the complimentary exposure at $12,000 for the 48-hour window. If you anticipate exceedance beyond that, please issue a PO for a provisional uplift and we'll provision an elevated temporary commit.

Next steps for BrightRetail: please send a PO referencing Deal BR-4831 (attachment stub if helpful) or confirm procurement contact and estimated peak qps. I will also share a DocuSign for the temporary uplift appendix if you want the credit/terms documented.

I've attached the pricing appendix for transparency.

Thanks and good luck with the launch — Connor will be on standby for any real-time routing or fallback setups.

Best,
